findings.summary: A FIFTH limit, MEASURED: a successor's own checkpoint carries NONE of the pod slots it inherited, so the SECOND takeover duplicates for every pod that did not commit to the middle leader. The DUPLICATED list names two; there are three, and this one needs no restart, no v0 object and no legacy build.
findings.detail:
The DUPLICATED family is derived from 'what a checkpoint cannot seed' and lists a superseded incarnation and a bare v0 slot. It misses what a checkpoint does not RECORD. CheckpointWriter.java:85 builds `pods` as a fresh empty HashMap and LocalSequencer.java:378 constructs the writer without ever handing it `log.recoveredPods()` (LocalSequencer.java:371 seeds only the in-memory IdempotencyWindow). The only writers of that map are `rememberPod` from `observe`/`observeReconciled`, i.e. commits made to THIS leader. So a checkpoint written at epoch E2 carries cumulative OFFSETS (ChainReplay.java:226-233 relies on exactly that) but a TRUNCATED pods map. ChainReplay.replayAncestry then stops the walk at that checkpoint (ChainReplay.java:193-196: crossFromCheckpoint returns true, applyChain, return), so epoch E1 is never read and every slot inherited from it is gone.

MEASURED on this tree, not inferred. Probe: L1(epoch 1) commits podb/i1 flushSeq 0 as seg/0; L1 closes; L2(epoch 2, K=1) commits two flushes from a DIFFERENT pod, so it writes its own checkpoint; L2 closes; L3(epoch 3) receives the retry of podb/i1 flushSeq 0 / seg/0. Result: no refusal, and `deltasCarrying(store, "seg/0") == 2` -- the same records at two offsets, which I2 forbids. CONTROL, same probe with the middle leader committing nothing (hence no checkpoint at epoch 2): 1 delta, the retry is handled correctly. So the mechanism is precisely the successor's own checkpoint, and it is neither of the two cases listed.

Why this blocks the task rather than being someone else's bug: the row exists because the list has been wrong three times, and the commit's own claim in src/main is that the list is now DERIVED from the code ('the two refusal branches of IdempotencyWindow.answer and ... what a checkpoint cannot seed') and that 'TWO of these duplicate'. Both statements are false as landed, and the fourth reader of this contract concludes that once v0 checkpoints age out of retention the only remaining duplication needs a pod restart -- when in fact it needs only a second takeover, which is normal operation on any rolling deploy. Fix is additive: name the case in the DUPLICATED list (it is UNPINNED) and open a backlog row for the production gap, the way the bare v0 slot has M5.22 and the superseded incarnation has M5.52. No split is implied; the diff is prose.
findings.failure_scenario: A rolling deploy moves the sequencer lease twice. Pod podb commits flushSeq 0 (seg/0) to the leader at epoch 1. The lease moves to epoch 2, which inherits podb's slot in memory but writes its own checkpoint carrying only the pods that committed to IT. The lease moves again to epoch 3, whose crossing stops at that checkpoint and never reads epoch 1. podb -- same incarnation, no restart, no v0 object anywhere -- retries flushSeq 0 after the lost reply, is treated as fresh, and the same records are committed at two offsets (I2). MEASURED on this tree: 2 deltas carry seg/0; with the middle leader writing no checkpoint the same probe gives 1.

findings.summary: The new 'stated by reference' sentence is one unwrapped 333-column line, and the commit's own stated exception to the column budget covers cited TEST NAMES only -- this line carries no identifier that has to grep.
findings.detail: Sequencer.java:77-83 records the deliberate exception: a cited Class.method must sit on one line so `grep` finds it. IdempotencyWindow.java:44 is prose -- 'STATED BY REFERENCE AND NOT RESTATED HERE -- with one exception ... {@link #seed}'s own javadoc below ...' -- at 333 characters, while every other line of that same javadoc block is wrapped at ~75. Failure scenario: the next edit to that sentence rewrites the whole 333-character line, so the line-based diff a reviewer is given shows one enormous changed line and the actual edit is invisible inside it. That is the review surface this repository's whole gate design rests on. Per review.md rule 11 this is recorded rather than fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits that sentence -- M5.52 closes the superseded-incarnation limit and the 'drift to watch' clause has to change. The staged diff shows one 333-character line replaced by another, so the reviewer bound to those bytes cannot see which clause moved, and a false claim slipped into the middle of it reads exactly like the surrounding unchanged prose.
